references.text: Herod expresses his confusion further and says, "Who then is this about whom I hear such things?" – a direct continuation of his reaction in verse 7.
Matthew's parallel account that the tetrarch Herod heard the report about Jesus and told his servants that it must be John the Baptist who had been raised from the dead.
Mark's parallel account where King Herod hears about Jesus, and people say that John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, while others say it is Elijah or one of the prophets.
Luke earlier tells us that Herod imprisoned John the Baptist, which forms the background for Herod's unease upon hearing about Jesus' deeds.
Matthew reports that Herod had John beheaded in prison, which explains why Herod now believes that John has been raised from the dead.
Mark's account of the execution of John the Baptist, which is the background for Herod's fear that John has risen again.
Jesus himself asks his disciples who people say he is, and they give answers similar to those Herod heard: John the Baptist, Elijah, or one of the old prophets.
Herod finally meets Jesus personally during the trial and had long wished to see him and hoped to witness a sign – a fulfillment of the curiosity that began in 9:7.
